<span class="section-index">02 / Philosophy</span>

## Structure Before Sophistication {#philosophy}

Most analytical problems do not begin with dashboards or models. They begin with questions. CentralStatz works through the structure behind the problem before building a solution.

Many organizations focus on output first. The stronger foundation is the system and reasoning that make an output trustworthy: transparent definitions, reproducible processes, defensible metrics, and maintainable implementation.

<div class="principle-grid">
  <div><strong>Clear questions</strong><span>Define what the work is meant to answer and support.</span></div>
  <div><strong>Defensible logic</strong><span>Make measures and assumptions open to review.</span></div>
  <div><strong>Reproducible systems</strong><span>Build work that can be understood, repeated, and maintained.</span></div>
  <div><strong>Appropriate tools</strong><span>Use sophistication only where the problem earns it.</span></div>
</div>

:::

## A place to investigate what analytical work could become.

The CentralStatz Lab turns carefully reasoned ideas into tangible prototypes, frameworks, and working systems that can be tested, challenged, and refined. It complements advisory work by making Alex’s approach to framing and building analytical systems visible—without making client work experimental by default.

<span class="section-index">04 / About</span>

## Meet Alex Zajichek

Alex is a statistician and data scientist in Central Wisconsin with more than a decade of experience learning, teaching, and doing data science work across tools, methods, and problem contexts.

His work is especially grounded in healthcare, where messy systems, consequential decisions, and fragile metrics make sound analytical structure essential. Through CentralStatz, he helps organizations build reproducible analytics, strengthen statistical reasoning, and create systems that make complex questions easier to answer over time.

```{=html}
<div id="submissionModal" class="modal" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="modalTitle" hidden>
  <div class="modal-content">
    <button type="button" class="close-modal" aria-label="Close dialog">&times;</button>
    <h3 id="modalTitle">What happens when I submit?</h3>
    <p>Your note goes directly to me at <a href="mailto:alex@centralstatz.com">alex@centralstatz.com</a>. I’ll review it and respond by email with any initial perspective I can offer. It is a connection point—not a commitment or obligation.</p>
    <p><strong>— Alex</strong></p>
  </div>
</div>
<script>
(() => {
  const modal = document.getElementById('submissionModal');
  const openButton = document.getElementById('openSubmissionModal');
  const closeButton = modal?.querySelector('.close-modal');
  let previousFocus;
  if (!modal || !openButton || !closeButton) return;
  const open = () => { previousFocus = document.activeElement; modal.hidden = false; document.body.classList.add('modal-open'); closeButton.focus(); };
  const close = () => { modal.hidden = true; document.body.classList.remove('modal-open'); previousFocus?.focus(); };
  openButton.addEventListener('click', open);
  closeButton.addEventListener('click', close);
  modal.addEventListener('click', event => { if (event.target === modal) close(); });
  document.addEventListener('keydown', event => { if (event.key === 'Escape' && !modal.hidden) close(); });
})();
</script>
```
